videos.description: The Thought Process of a Data Scientist 👩‍💻 I didn’t start by building the deepest neural network possible - I started by understanding the 120,000 images and how the model would learn the difference between real and AI-generated content. Because the dataset contained an equal number of real and fake images, accuracy gave me a meaningful overall measurement, but I also tracked precision, recall, and ROC-AUC to understand the mistakes hidden behind that number. The network gradually learns more complicated visual patterns through three convolutional layers, while pooling, normalization, and dropout help it train efficiently and generalize to unseen images. In the end, the model reached 87.95% test accuracy and a 0.975 ROC-AUC—but it still made mistakes, which is an important reminder that an AI detector produces a probability, not absolute proof. Building a proof-of-concept AI agent can be done in a single script. But moving that agent into production? That requires a robust, scalable architecture. If you are transitioning from basic LLM scripts to engineering production-grade agents, keeping your codebase clean is half the battle. Here is a battle-tested blueprint for an AI Agent Project Structure that keeps your code modular, maintainable, and highly testable: 📂 The Core Breakdown  * agent/ (The Brain): Houses your core agent logic, execution loops, state management, and memory handling. Keep this isolated from specific tool implementations.  * tools/ (The Capabilities): Where your agent's superpowers live. Separate your search, calculation, or external API calling scripts into standalone, modular tools.  * models/ (The Engines): Manages your LLM and embedding client configurations. If you switch from OpenAI to Anthropic or an open-source model, this is the only place you should need to touch.  * prompts/ (The Instructions): Never hardcode prompts into your application logic. Dedicate a folder to system and agent prompt templates to make iterating on prompt engineering seamless.  * api/ (The Gateway): Wraps your agent into an API layer (using FastAPI, Flask, etc.) so it can easily integrate with frontend apps or external microservices.  * tests/, data/, & logs/ (The Production Guardrails): Essential for evaluating agent performance, tracking execution paths, and catching edge cases before they hit production. > 💡 Pro-Tip: Notice the .env file in the root? Always use it to manage your LLM API keys and environment variables, and ensure it is included in your .gitignore so secrets are never pushed to GitHub! >  How do you structure your AI projects? Do you prefer a monolithic approach early on, or do you start modular from day one? Let’s discuss in the comments below! 👇 #AIAgents #ArtificialIntelligence #SoftwareEngineering #Python #LLM

slideshows.description: Claude just released Sonnet 5, and the short version is that near-flagship AI is now the free default, so here's everything you actually need to know. Sonnet 5 is Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet model yet, which means it doesn't just chat back, it makes a plan, uses tools like a browser and a terminal, finishes multi-step tasks, and checks its own work. It landed on June 30 and is now the default model on the Free and Pro plans, so if you use claude.ai you're most likely already on it. The real story is the value. Sonnet 5 closes most of the gap with Opus 4.8, Claude's top-tier flagship, while costing a fraction of the price. Introductory pricing is 2 dollars per million input tokens and 10 per million output through August 31, then 3 and 15 after that. Here's how it stacks up against Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.8 (higher is better): - Agentic coding, SWE-bench Pro: 63.2% vs 58.1% vs 69.2% - Agentic coding, Terminal-Bench 2.1: 80.4% vs 67.0% vs 82.7% - Reasoning, Humanity's Last Exam (with tools): 57.4% vs 46.8% vs 57.9% - Computer use, OSWorld-Verified: 81.2% vs 78.5% vs 83.4% - Knowledge work, GDPval-AA v2: 1618 vs 1395 vs 1615 Read that last row again, because Sonnet 5 actually edges out Opus on knowledge work. Across the board it beats Sonnet 4.6 comfortably and lands within a point or two of the flagship on almost everything. So when do you use which? Reach for Sonnet 5 for everyday work, coding, automation, research, and analysis, which is to say almost everything, at the best price. Reach for Opus 4.8 only for the hardest frontier tasks where every point counts, or specialised work like security research where you need the absolute ceiling. What it means for you is simple: your free default just got a lot smarter with no upgrade and no setup, you get near-flagship quality without paying flagship prices, and because it's agentic it can actually do multi-step tasks rather than just answer. The bar for "good enough AI" moved up, for free. Save this so you know which model to reach for next time. #ai #productivity #claude #chatgpt #claudesonnet5

slideshows.description: AI makes real PowerPoints — not images, not templates, but natively editable PPTX files you can actually work with. Most AI presentation tools either fill in rigid templates or flatten each slide into a giant image you can't touch. PPT Master takes a different approach: feed it any document (PDF, HTML, markdown) and it generates a real PowerPoint file with native shapes, text boxes, charts, and animations — all fully clickable and editable. It runs as a workflow inside AI IDEs like Claude Code or Cursor. You literally ask the AI to "make a deck from this PDF" and it produces a .pptx on your machine. No upload, no SaaS subscription, no lock-in. The project is open source (MIT) with 33K GitHub stars and supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi, and other models. Built by Hugo He, a finance professional who was tired of AI-generated slides being flattened into uneditable images. The results speak for themselves — 21 example decks ranging from academic paper readings on Transformers to glassmorphism SaaS pitch decks, all generated in a single pass. #AI #PowerPoint #OpenSource #DevTools #Productivity

CLAUDE.md Loaded every single session.
Project overview, tech stack, coding conventions, architecture notes, hard rules, and
safety boundaries. Under 200 lines-every line earns its space.
CLAUDE.local.md Personal overrides. Never committed.
Your machine-specific paths, personal preferences, and experimental rules.
Gitignored. Stacks on top of CLAUDE.md - never replaces it.
AGENTS.md The team roster. Who does what.
Defines every subagent's role, capabilities, and handoff protocol. Claude reads this
before delegating. Prevents overlap. Keeps multi-agent sessions coordinated.
mcp.json MCP server integrations. Shared via git.
Connects Claude to GitHub, Notion, Slack, Gmail, PostgreSQL, Jira, and 200+ tools
settings.json Permissions, tools, and hooks config.
Defines what Claude can read, write, and execute. Allow and deny lists. Hook events
wired here. Committed to git-personal overrides go in settings.local.json.
rules/md-Modular rule files. Loaded on demand.
Each .md is a focused rule module code style, API conventions, testing standards, PR
format. Keeps CLAUDE.md lean by externalizing detail that only loads when relevant.
commands/*.md Custom slash commands for your project.
Each.md becomes a/project.command-name. Supports SARGUMENTS for user input.
Perfect for PR reviews, deploys, and scaffolding. Type / in chat to see all commands.
skills/<name>/SKILL.md-Auto-triggered by task context.
Not a single file-a directory per skill. The description field is the routing rule. Loads
only when Claude recognizes the task. One job per Skill. Keeps context lightweight.
agents/md-Specialized subagents with isolated context.
Own system prompt, own tools, own permissions. Runs in a separate context
window-research without polluting main session. Invoke with @agent-name.
hooks/sh Event-driven scripts. 100% enforcement.
Make sure Claude does something deterministically via shell commands - not LLM
interpretation. PreToolUse blocks. PostTooluse reacts. Exit 0 allow. Exit 2 block
memory/.md-Persistent ent memory across all sessions.
Project context, architectural decisions, and progress logs Claude reads between
sessions. Compensates for context loss in long projects. Commit to git-the
whole team benefits.
workflows/*.md-Multi-step task blueprints.
Each .md defines a repeatable workflow feature build, bug fix, code review
cycle. Claude follows the blueprint step by step. Combines Skills, Subagents, and
Hooks in sequence.
